quarterly_data.quarter: Alamar Biosciences press release: Lancet Neurology Study Using Alamar Biosciences' Technology (09-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The company announced publication in The Lancet Neurology of what it calls the first longitudinal cohort study to evaluate a broad panel of plasma biomarkers in patients receiving anti-amyloid antibody therapy (lecanemab) in real-world clinical practice. Led by Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis investigators, the study used Alamar's NULISAseq CNS 120 panel to measure 130 plasma proteins, profiling 2,385 samples from 1,967 participants with just 25 microliters of plasma per sample. Results stated by the company: proteins associated with amyloid clearance were largely different from those associated with subsequent cognitive decline; among 197 lecanemab-treated patients, 34 of the 130 biomarkers significantly changed with the number of infusions, not all in the same direction; and brain-derived forms of tau consistently outperformed the same proteins circulating in the periphery, accounting for four of the top five proteins distinguishing these patients from controls both before treatment and at the last infusion stage. The company says measuring these variants alongside more than 100 additional proteins in a single sample is what allowed the investigators to track pathology and treatment response in one assay. CEO: the study shows why measuring one or two biomarkers is not enough to understand treatment and why ultra-high sensitivity matters.
